clue.text: One bearing inwards, we hear

parts.note: read 'inwards' as if heard as 'in wards': a hospital worker who carries patients about the wards of the building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inwards' spoken sounds like 'in wards', and the person who bears (carries) patients and supplies within hospital wards is the porter there.
explanation.definitionFit: This orderly wheels and carries patients between departments, so bearing them about the wards is the job itself.

clue.text: Taking to water, Sunday opening suffering!

indicators.note: the opening of the word Sunday is its first letter, which starts the answer

parts.note: someone suffering is ailing, unwell

explanation.surface: A grumble that a Sunday trip on the water began with seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Going out on a boat under canvas is taking to the water.

clue.text: Model incomplete for plan

indicators.note: incomplete means the synonym for model loses its last letter here

parts.note: a model, perfect example, is an ideal

explanation.surface: An unfinished model is offered in place of a proper scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or scheme in someone's mind is a notion of what to do.

clue.text: True bass arrangement difficult to follow

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks material, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician complains that a faithful arrangement for bass is hard to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' sounds musical beside 'bass', but it shuffles the letters of TRUE and BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure and recondite is hard for the mind to grasp.

clue.text: His ware, by the way, interested Simple Simon

definitions.text: His ware, by the way, interested Simple Simon

parts.words: His ware, by the way, interested Simple Simon
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Simple Simon meets a seller going to the fair and asks to taste his ware

explanation.walkthrough: The English nursery rhyme runs 'Simple Simon met a pieman going to the fair; said Simple Simon to the pieman, let me taste your ware'. 'By the way' is his roadside meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's roadside vendor sells pastry goods, which is what caught Simon's eye.

clue.text: US politician has all the people in near-collapse

indicators.note: in places the people's word inside the jumbled letters
a collapse leaves things in a heap, so the letters of near fall into disorder

parts.note: the public is everyone, all the people

explanation.surface: A US politician gets the whole nation in a near-collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near-collapse' reads as one phrase, an almost-breakdown, but splits: 'collapse' jumbles the word before it, and 'in' houses the people inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two main US parties is Republican, so a member of it is a politician.

clue.text: Try to keep up with English musicians behind the beat

parts.note: MU is the Musicians' Union, a British trade union
playing behind the beat is playing late

explanation.surface: A band struggles to keep pace, its English players lagging behind the rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: MU, the Musicians' Union, is the UK trade union for performers.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to imitate or rival someone, striving to equal them.

clue.text: Tolerant of things made to standard sizes

explanation.surface: A shopper accepting off-the-peg clothes rather than tailored ones.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage to 'wear' something is to put up with it ('the boss won't wear that'), so someone willing to tolerate things is in that state.
explanation.definitionFit: Willing to accept something is one sense; the other is clothing sold off the peg in fixed sizes rather than tailored.

clue.text: Lice seen swarming around host

indicators.note: insects swarming around move in a chaotic mass, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pub landlord finds his premises infested with lice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' is the landlord of a pub, who holds a licence to sell drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of a pub's drinks licence is the landlord who welcomes guests.

clue.text: Pop profit by such a break?

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, pa
to profit by something is to use it

explanation.surface: A suggestion that Dad might benefit from a short rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief stop or interval is a break in activity.

clue.text: Privileged people travelling to Carstairs

indicators.note: letters travelling move around, so to and Carstairs are rearranged

explanation.surface: The gentry heading off to Carstairs, a Scottish town and rail junction.
explanation.walkthrough: Carstairs is a village and railway junction in Lanarkshire, Scotland; 'travelling' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the nobility are a privileged upper class.

clue.text: Game at home at Tintern for instance

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a ball game
in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: A match played at home at Tintern, a Welsh village.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintern Abbey in the Wye valley of Wales is a famous roofless remains of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern Abbey is a celebrated example of a decayed, roofless old building.

clue.text: Pay tribunal's base for doing the rounds?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, pay
a board is a body that sits in judgement, a tribunal

explanation.surface: An employment panel set up to rule on wages for staff on their rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like patrols or deliveries, but means rounds of bread, slices or sandwiches, which are cut on a wooden base.
explanation.definitionFit: Slices (rounds) of a loaf are cut on this wooden board in the kitchen.

clue.text: Shows women listen to the fashion at Wimbledon!

parts.note: to sport something is to show it off
to give ear is to listen

explanation.surface: Female players displaying the latest look at the Wimbledon tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London grass-court tennis tournament, so its fashion is clothing for athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing designed for athletic games is what tennis players wear on court.

clue.text: Army" signaller by the way

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Army" signaller by the way' carries a stray quote mark; 'signaller by the way' defines a roadside sign, but 'Army' has no job in any parse, so the printed clue appears garbled.

clue.text: To strip very rich man takes time

parts.note: Dives is the rich man of the parable of Lazarus in Luke's gospel

explanation.surface: A millionaire takes his time removing his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives (Latin for 'rich') is the traditional name of the rich man in Jesus's parable of Dives and Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to deprive or remove, as of clothing or possessions.

clue.text: Abandoning farmwork?

explanation.definitionFit: Dumping something is one sense; the other is digging and clearing drainage trenches on farmland.

clue.text: Workers not opening tankers from OPEC?

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the workers' word is removed

parts.note: toilers are people who work hard

explanation.surface: Workers refusing to unlock oil tankers from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: OPEC is the oil producers' cartel, so its tankers carry oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships carrying crude oil are known as oilers, a term for tanker vessels.

clue.text: Ring different hotels in the country

indicators.note: something different is changed, so the letters of hotels are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Call up several hotels in rural areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a telephone call but gives the round letter, set after the rearranged hotels; 'the country' looks like countryside but is a southern African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a kingdom in southern Africa entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Refuse girl's grant

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, here with the possessive S
to grant is to allow

explanation.surface: A request to turn down a young woman's application for funding.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow something is to reject or forbid it.

clue.text: Hangs around Oriel St, aimlessly

indicators.note: moving aimlessly means wandering about without order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone drifting around Oriel Street in Oxford with no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college; 'aimlessly' rearranges ORIEL and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingering idly in a place is hanging about.

clue.text: Banger regrettably reverses on motorway

indicators.note: reverses means the word for regrettably is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning regrettably
M1, written MI, is Britain's main motorway north from London

explanation.surface: A banger, a battered old car, sadly reversing on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' suggests an old car on the motorway, but is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is British slang for a sausage, of which a spicy cured kind is one.

clue.text: Fighting back in the underground?

explanation.definitionFit: Opposition to attack is one sense; the other is a secret wartime movement opposing an occupier.

clue.text: Tuscan site of listed building

parts.note: 'listed' read as leaning or tilting rather than officially protected: the Tuscan city of the famous tilted tower

explanation.walkthrough: A 'listed building' in Britain is one protected for its historic value; here 'listed' means leaning, as a ship lists.
explanation.definitionFit: This Tuscan city is home to the famous Leaning Tower.

clue.text: Head of Music on the guitar

definitions.text: Head of Music on the guitar

parts.words: Head of Music on the guitar
parts.note: Italian for head, a clamp fitted across the guitar neck to raise the pitch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Music' looks like a school department head, but the word is Italian for head, used for a guitar clamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A movable bar clamped on a guitar's fingerboard takes its name from the Italian for head.

clue.text: It has to go back by the tenth

indicators.note: to go back means the word it is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: A suggestion that something is returned by the tenth of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns IT into TI, followed by THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the church.

clue.text: As dynamic as Donald Duck, for example

explanation.definitionFit: Lively and spirited is one sense; the other is a cartoon character made to move on screen.

clue.text: Duo has sobering effect in digs!

indicators.note: to effect change on these words is to rework them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people find their lodgings have a sobering influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' is British slang for rented lodgings; 'effect' signals rearranging DUO, HAS and SOBERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs are lodgings, and guesthouses offering room and meals are a classic kind.
